prompt: Repair the replay package's in-memory topic broker. Keep the existing exported API, including New(retain int), Broker.Subscribe(topic string, after uint64, buffer int), Publish(topic string, payload []byte), Close() error, and Subscription.C, Cancel(), Err(). New rejects negative retention with ErrInvalid; zero retention is valid. Topics are independent exact nonempty strings; their successful publishes have consecutive sequences starting at 1. Keep only the newest retain messages per topic. Subscribe atomically replays retained messages with Sequence > after, then joins live delivery without gaps/duplicates. For an existing topic let latest be its last sequence and earliest cursor be latest - number of retained messages. Reject after > latest with ErrCursor, after < earliest cursor with ErrExpired, and replay count > buffer with ErrBacklog. An unseen topic has latest=0. Buffer must be >=1. Argument validation (empty topic/invalid buffer) precedes closed-state checks and returns ErrInvalid. Other Subscribe/Publish calls after broker close return ErrClosed (Publish returns sequence 0 on error). Every subscriber receives its own payload copy; changing publisher buffers after Publish returns or one delivered message must not alter another subscriber or replay history. Publish must never wait for a consumer: if a subscriber buffer is full, detach it, close its channel, and set its terminal Err to ErrSlow; do not enqueue the overflowing message for that subscriber, but the publish still succeeds, enters history, and reaches other subscribers. Cancel is idempotent, closes its channel, detaches it and leaves Err nil unless it already terminated for another reason. Close is idempotent and returns nil; it closes active subscribers with ErrClosed, preserving any earlier terminal reason. Closing never discards queued messages. Err is nil for active subscriptions. All operations are linearizable and race-free, including concurrent Publish/Subscribe/Cancel/Close/Err; once Cancel returns no later messages may be enqueued for it. The tests run with go test -race. Add regression coverage; no network or background persistence is needed.
